clue.text: The credit side of thrift? Not officially!

definitions.note: the definition is adverbial, describing trade done off the books, while the answer is the noun naming that trade

parts.note: an account with money in it is in the black, so black is the credit side
economy is careful, thrifty use of money

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether the reward for saving money is ever officially recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a cryptic reading: 'in the black' means in credit, hence BLACK, and thrift is ECONOMY. The definition is the exclamation, describing trade done unofficially.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash-in-hand trade that dodges tax and regulation is carried on unofficially, outside the recorded economy.

clue.text: What clergy need for surviving on Sunday

parts.note: living means staying alive, surviving

explanation.surface: A remark that the clergy depend on Sunday collections to get by.
explanation.walkthrough: A clergyman's 'living' is his benefice, the paid church post; 'on' places S after LIVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are appointed to benefices, church posts that come with an income, traditionally called livings.

clue.text: By which we judge one in erratic performance

indicators.note: a performance here is a display or rigmarole that churns up the letters around it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judge explaining the standards by which an erratic performer is assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I (one) with the letters of ERRATIC, and 'performance' rearranges the whole pool into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards or tests used in reaching a judgement are its basis of assessment.

clue.text: Saw the old editor outside

indicators.note: outside says the archaic word wraps around the abbreviation for editor

parts.note: ye is an old form of 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone spotted the former editor standing outside the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' looks like a description of the editor, but it stands for the archaic spelling of 'the', which goes outside the editor's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eyed something is to have looked at it, the past tense of seeing.

clue.text: Educated old boy starts to rub out

indicators.note: starts says the old boy's letters begin the answer, ahead of the word for educated

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a British school
literate means able to read and write, educated

explanation.surface: A well-schooled former pupil begins erasing something.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school; 'starts' puts his abbreviation first, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or erase completely.

clue.text: Alright! A Greek letter game

parts.note: OK is an exclamation of agreement, alright
pi is the sixteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to a game involving Greek letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is not a pastime here but a wild animal hunted or watched, here a striped African forest mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means wild animals, and this giraffe relative of the Congo forests is one.

clue.text: Finally figures out when!

parts.note: read as the moment when a business's figures are finally worked out, the point at which annual accounts are closed

explanation.surface: Someone at last works out the timing of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person puzzling out a date; the cryptic reading is the time of year when the accounts (figures) are finalised.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of a financial twelve-month period is when the accounts are drawn up and totalled.

clue.text: The case for tactful reserve

parts.note: diplomatic means tactful and discreet
to bag something is to claim or reserve it, as in bagging a seat

explanation.surface: An argument in favour of polite discretion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The case' looks like 'the argument' but is a physical container: the sealed pouch that carries an embassy's official mail, immune from search.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed container for official correspondence sent between a government and its embassies is a kind of case.

clue.text: A brave move-like a panther jumping over top of door

indicators.note: jumping suggests the letters leap about into a new order
the top of a down-reading word is its first letter, so take the first letter of door

explanation.surface: Something bold, like a big cat leaping over a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' rearranges LIKE, A PANTHER and D, the top of 'door'; 'over' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: An action taken without knowing its outcome is a bold venture into the unknown.

clue.text: Bill's at home, say

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
to voice something is to say it

explanation.surface: Bill is at home, someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a request for payment; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A document listing what a customer owes for goods or services is a bill.

clue.text: Loss suffered from meadow enclosure is listened to

indicators.note: is listened to says the words must be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: a lea is a meadow and a cage is an enclosure, together LEA CAGE

explanation.surface: Someone hears about losses suffered from a fenced field.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA (meadow) plus CAGE (enclosure), spoken, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak lets fluid or information escape, so the amount escaping is a loss.

clue.text: Weapon's point absorbed by material

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the material word

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric, a material
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The tip of a weapon has soaked into some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like the weapon's tip but is a compass point, N, put inside LACE; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by a mounted knight is a weapon.

clue.text: Initiate walk out at university

parts.note: workers who walk out are on strike
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Students start a walkout on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' is British usage for being in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin a conversation or friendship is to initiate it.

clue.text: Change clue ending in gratification

indicators.note: Change tells us to alter the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A setter changes the end of a clue to please themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges the ten letters of CLUE ENDING; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing yourself a pleasure is gratifying a desire.

clue.text: Word from him, when abroad

parts.note: read Word as the Gospel: someone sent abroad who brings the Word of God to foreign lands

explanation.surface: A traveller sends news home from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word' with a capital is the Christian message, which the person sent overseas carries to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher sent to other countries to spread the Christian Gospel is an evangelist abroad.

clue.text: Last to leave study for garden

indicators.note: Last to means the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: The last person out leaves the study for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last to leave' reads as the last person going, but it is the final letter of 'leave'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived is the archetypal garden.

clue.text: Clearance obtained from chief before African uprising

indicators.note: before puts the word for chief ahead of the reversed piece in this down clue

parts.note: head means chief, leader

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a Moor is a North African

explanation.surface: A space cleared after a rebellion in Africa led by a chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' sounds like a revolt, but in a down entry it turns MOOR upwards to give ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The space above your head, as under a bridge or in a car, is the clearance.

clue.text: Put back time trial

indicators.note: back says the word for put is read the other way round

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A time trial is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' looks like 'postpone', but 'back' turns only the word for put, and time's abbreviation follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is a trial or examination of something.

clue.text: Partners fly in for a bit

indicators.note: in puts the insect inside the partners' letters

parts.note: in bridge, South and North play as partners, S and N
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: A couple fly in to stay for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like a verb but is a small insect, MIDGE, placed between S and N, bridge partners; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny quantity is a little bit.

clue.text: Manage to find truth -are no letters exchanged?

indicators.note: letters exchanged says the letters of the words before swap places

explanation.surface: A question about whether truth can be found without swapping letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters exchanged' rearranges TRUTH ARE NO; the question form disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: To track something down after a long search, as hounds chase a fox to its hole, is finally to locate it.

clue.text: Make coarse opening remark on huge letters

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of remark
letters says the following words are only raw letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes a crude remark about big letters.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the opening of 'remark', is followed by ON and HUGE rearranged, the 'letters' rearranging them.
explanation.definitionFit: To roughen a surface is to make it less smooth.

clue.text: Take the mickey out of reserve in church game

indicators.note: in puts the two words inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to rib someone is to tease them, taking the mickey in British slang
to bag is to reserve, as in bagging a seat

explanation.surface: Someone teases a reserve player at a church games night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the mickey out of' is British slang for tease; 'reserve' looks like a substitute player but is a verb, as in bagging a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game scored on a pegboard is a game.

clue.text: Under the Spanish, protected by inclination

indicators.note: protected by puts the article inside the word for inclination

parts.note: a bow is an inclination of the head or body
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish people under the protection of someone's inclination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' looks like a tendency but is a bending of the body, BOW, protecting EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneath another thing lies under it.

clue.text: Priest fiddled game inside

indicators.note: inside says the game's letters sit within the word for fiddled

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them, so did means fiddled
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A priest cheated during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did' is British slang for cheated (fiddled); RU, rugby union, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient Celtic priesthood was a priest.

clue.text: A Yankee's help

parts.note: a Yankee is a type of multiple bet on horses

explanation.surface: An American is offering assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yankee is a British bookmakers' wager of eleven bets on four horses, not an American; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, chiefly in wrongdoing.

clue.text: African backing record in two articles

indicators.note: in puts the reversed record between the articles

parts.note: an and an are two indefinite articles

indicators.note: backing means the word for record is read backwards

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An African supporter keeps a record in two pieces of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for an African but signals a reversal of the word for record, which sits between the two articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Angola, a country in southwest Africa, is an African.

clue.text: Run in to trouble one's companion

indicators.note: in to puts the abbreviation inside the word for trouble

parts.note: bother means trouble
R is the abbreviation for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A friend runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: R (run) goes inside BOTHER; 'one's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow member or comrade is a companion, as in brothers in arms.

clue.text: Fresh examination meant reordering books

parts.note: new means fresh
a test is an examination

indicators.note: reordering means putting the letters of the word meant into another order

explanation.surface: A new exam has meant rearranging the textbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reordering' rearranges MEANT to AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The second part of the Christian Bible is a collection of twenty-seven books.
